high.title: Bursa retreats as market digests latest US tariffs
high.summary: The FBM KLCI fell amid escalating geopolitical tensions, with Brent crude oil breaching US$100 per barrel following attacks on Saudi oil tankers and renewed US strikes on Iran. The combination of new US tariffs and surging oil prices is weighing on investor sentiment and raising inflation and global growth concerns. The 1,700 level is seen as a key technical support for the index.

high.title: Ringgit ends slightly lower amid Middle East tensions, US tariffs
high.summary: The ringgit weakened as Asian currencies traded mixed amid uncertainty over crude oil prices and new US tariffs, including a 10% forced labour-related tariff on Malaysian exports that took effect today. The Strait of Hormuz blockade is adding upward pressure on oil prices, elevating external risks and boosting demand for the US dollar. Malaysia's Miti is continuing engagement with the US over the newly imposed tariff.

high.title: Bursa opens lower amid cautious market sentiment
high.summary: The FBM KLCI opened lower, retreating over 6 points as Brent crude surpassed US$100 per barrel and Wall Street's Nasdaq dropped 2.15% following disappointing reactions to Alphabet's and Tesla's spending plans. Broader market breadth was negative with losers significantly outpacing gainers. The confluence of geopolitical risks and tech sector weakness is creating a challenging environment for Malaysian equities.

high.title: Ringgit opens higher against major currencies, softer vs US dollar
high.summary: The ringgit weakened against the US dollar to 4.0925/4.0980 as Trump announced new import tariffs of 10%-12.5% on 60 economies including Malaysia, citing forced labour practices. This follows a US Supreme Court annulment of previous tariff measures, signalling continued trade policy uncertainty. The ringgit is expected to trade cautiously in the RM4.08-RM4.10 range, with significant implications for Malaysian exporters and trade-dependent businesses.

high.title: Ringgit ends lower amid Middle East tensions
high.summary: The ringgit eased to 4.0870/4.0910 against the USD as escalating Middle East conflicts drove Brent crude up 4.23% to US$98.05/barrel, raising global inflationary concerns. The probability of a US Fed rate hike in September jumped to 64.8% from 51.5% in early July, strengthening the US dollar index. These developments have major implications for Malaysian monetary policy, import costs, and currency stability.

high.title: Ringgit ends higher against US dollar, other currencies amid rising oil prices
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0850/4.0890 against the USD as Brent crude surged above US$94 per barrel, significantly up from US$71.57 on July 1, 2026. Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong highlighted that every US$1 rise in oil prices generates an additional RM300 million in government revenue. US-Iran conflict escalation and Trump's 100% tariff on generic drugs add further complexity to market dynamics.

high.title: Bursa ends lower amid profit-taking, higher oil prices
high.summary: The FBM KLCI fell 9 points (0.52%) to 1,711.37, driven by profit-taking after a strong rally from around 1,655 to 1,735. Elevated crude oil prices above US$94/barrel and Houthi threats to widen Middle East conflict weighed on risk appetite across regional markets. Analysts suggest the pullback may offer bargain-hunting opportunities in fundamentally sound large-cap stocks.

high.title: Ringgit opens almost flat amid Middle East uncertainty
high.summary: The ringgit opened nearly unchanged at 4.0870/4.0920 as the US-Iran conflict entered its tenth day, heightening geopolitical uncertainty. Rising US Treasury yields (2-year at 4.26%, 10-year at 4.63%) signal growing expectations of a US interest rate hike, which could impact capital flows to Malaysia. Traders are expected to remain cautious with the ringgit trading in the RM4.08–RM4.10 range.

high.title: Singapore Leads Record Foreign Investments in Southeast Asia
high.summary: FDI to Southeast Asia hit a record US$244 billion in 2025, with Malaysia posting the strongest regional growth at 51%, driven primarily by digital infrastructure investments. This signals strong investor confidence in Malaysia's economy and positions it as a key beneficiary of global capital flows. Malaysian investors should take note of the continued momentum in the digital and tech sectors as key drivers of economic expansion.

medium.title: Westports outperforms despite Middle East fallout
medium.summary: Westports posted a strong Q2 FY2026 net profit jump of 56% to RM360.9 million despite elevated fuel costs driven by Middle East conflict, with H1 revenue rising 34% to RM1.76 billion. The results beat analyst expectations, prompting most research houses to maintain 'buy' calls on the stock. The outperformance signals resilience in Malaysia's port sector even amid global supply chain disruptions.

medium.title: Khazanah said to sell US$340mil Tenaga stake in placement
medium.summary: Khazanah Nasional is reported to have sold 100 million Tenaga Nasional shares at RM13.91 each, at a 4.5% discount to market price, in a placement deal worth approximately US$340 million. The sale reduces Khazanah's stake in one of Malaysia's largest listed companies and may signal a strategic portfolio rebalancing by the sovereign wealth fund. The placement could create short-term selling pressure on Tenaga shares.

medium.title: Bursa snaps 3-day losing streak to end higher
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 3.22 points to 1,714.59, breaking a three-day losing streak driven by buying interest in oil and gas and utilities sectors amid rising global oil prices. However, broader market sentiment remained cautious with decliners outnumbering advancers 599 to 415 and turnover declining to RM2.27 billion. The selective recovery reflects ongoing investor uncertainty despite positive energy sector momentum.

medium.title: Bursa opens higher on global tech earnings spillover
medium.summary: Bursa Malaysia opened higher with the FBM KLCI gaining 3.42 points to 1,714.79, supported by positive spillover from Alphabet's strong Q2 FY2026 results driven by Google Cloud growth. Gainers outpaced losers 203 to 134 in early trade, suggesting cautious optimism among investors. The global tech earnings season continues to influence sentiment on local technology-linked counters.

medium.title: Ringgit eases against US dollar, tracks major currencies
medium.summary: The ringgit opened slightly softer at 4.0855/4.0920 against the USD, though analysts noted its relative resilience due to Malaysia's strong trade data and energy exporter status providing a buffer against broader dollar strength. Rising odds of a September US Fed rate hike to 64.8% are reinforcing dollar-positive sentiment in the near term. Malaysia's improving terms of trade offer some protection but currency pressure is expected to persist.

medium.title: Blackstone lines up US$3bil AirTrunk loan as data centre debt concerns grow
medium.summary: Blackstone is arranging a US$3 billion loan for AirTrunk to build the SYD3 hyperscale data centre, with regional banks including DBS and UOB among the lenders. This deal is part of a broader surge in AI infrastructure financing, with at least US$334.5 billion raised globally in 2026, nearly double the 2025 total. Malaysian investors should note growing data centre investment momentum in the Asia-Pacific region and potential opportunities in related sectors.

medium.title: Bursa opens slightly lower as profit-taking caps gains
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened slightly lower at 1,713.79, with profit-taking offsetting positive momentum from Wall Street's rally led by semiconductor stocks and strong corporate earnings. Broader market breadth remained positive with gainers outpacing losers at 237 to 153. The mixed open reflects cautious investor sentiment balancing global tech optimism against ongoing Middle East geopolitical risks.

medium.title: Ringgit Extends Gains on Stronger Trade Performance
medium.summary: The ringgit is extending gains supported by a rebound in Asian semiconductor stocks and stronger trade performance, even as the US dollar strengthens across G10 currencies. Analysts expect a steady, slightly positive bias for the ringgit through the week, with the primary downside risk being a geopolitical escalation in West Asia that could trigger a safe-haven USD rally. Malaysian businesses with USD-denominated exposure should monitor geopolitical developments closely.
